add.title: Guardian: Ireland's gender recognition act, a decade on (The Guardian)
add.summary: Guardian (23 Dec 2025) decade retrospective on the 2015 Gender Recognition Act: it documents the Barbie Kardashian case — a violent offender who changed name by deed poll and obtained a gender recognition certificate in 2020, then was transferred from a women's prison to a male prison during her sentence — as the case that made prison custody a focus of gender-critical campaigning in Ireland, and reports that an amendment to the GRA 'which would limit its scope so the certificate no longer changes sex for the purposes of imprisonment' has passed its first stage in the Oireachtas; the amendment was drafted by barrister Laoise de Brun (of The Countess), who cites UK gender-critical campaigners as inspiration.

add.title: Transgender history in Ireland (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Wikipedia 'Transgender history in Ireland' (rev. 2 Oct 2026): documents Barbie Kardashian, a trans woman who held a Gender Recognition Certificate and a Department of Social Protection certificate recognising her as female — found guilty at Limerick Circuit Court in May 2022 of seven counts of threatening to kill or cause serious harm to her mother, and acquitted in October 2024 of separate alleged threats to a fellow prisoner and a prison officer at Limerick Prison; the article records that as of late 2025 a proposed amendment to the Gender Recognition Act 2015 that would limit the effect of a GRC 'for the purposes of imprisonment' had passed its first legislative stage, and cites the historical 1889 case of John Bradley (assigned female at birth), imprisoned at Grangegorman prison after disclosing.
